newsitem.title: USA: Benetton sells sport eyewear unit to Bausch.
newsitem.headline: Benetton sells sport eyewear unit to Bausch.

text.p: Optical giant Bausch & Lomb Inc. has bought Killer Loop Eyewear, Benetton Sportsystem SpA's sunglass maker, whose products sport names like "Vicious" and "Pandemonium," the companies announced Monday.
The purchase price was not disclosed.

Rochester, N.Y.-based Bausch & Lomb, which had been the sole worldwide distribution agent for the sports sunglasses, is now 100 percent owner of Killer Loop Eyewear, including its trademark and its design and development unit in Pederobba, Italy.
Benetton Sportsystem retains its interest in Killer Loop clothing, accessories and sporting goods like snowboards, the Italian company said.
"We have chosen to concentrate on what we do best: street apparel, sportswear and sporting goods," Benetton Sportsystem Chairman Gilberto Benetton said in a statement.

"Forecasts show these are the market sectors offering the greatest scope for development. We will continue to design, manufacture and market our Killer Loop apparel and sporting goods and we will expand these businesses," he said.
Bausch & Lomb said it would retain Killer Loop's work force of 115 people.

"We can now reap the full reward of the investments we've made over the years in developing this fast-growing brand," W. Jeff Pontius, vice president and global business manager for Bausch & Lomb Eyewear, said in the statement.
Killer Loop Eyewear is targeted at 18- to 34-year-old active males.
